newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River tow breaks up near Baton Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River tow breaks up near Baton Rouge.

text.p: A 20-barge tow broke up on the Mississippi River upriver from the Interstate 90 bridge near here on Tuesday, temporarily halting traffic through this section of the river, a U.S. Coast Guard spokesman said.
The early afternoon accident occured near the site where crews were working to right another barge that capsized last week loaded with a volatile cargo of benzene and gasoline, he said.
"Traffic is stopped, but the barges have been contained," the Coast Guard spokesman said. He could not estimate when restricted traffic could resume in the area.
Shipping has been restricted to a one-way, one-vessel or tow at a time in the area of the March 17 accident in which a tow of 25 barges hit the bridge.

There have been several accidents on the river as pilots cope with fast-moving, flood-swollen currents that have swept away barges and caused one freighter to ground in a deep-draft channel at the mouth of the river last week.
